iosAutomation.title: iOS Automation
iosAutomation.description: Log your card payments in MoneyMatter without typing anything. An iOS Shortcut sends each Apple Pay tap and, on iOS 27 or later, the notifications your banks send, and MoneyMatter files them on the account linked to the card.
iosAutomation.manualGuide: Prefer to build the shortcut by hand? Follow the {link}.

setup.title: Shortcut setup
setup.description: Generate a setup code, add the shortcut that matches your iPhone and paste the code when the shortcut asks for it. The code carries a new token, so nothing else needs to be typed.
setup.revokePreviousHint: The shortcut that uses the old token stops working until you set it up again with the new code.
setup.generateError: Could not generate the setup code
setup.shareShortcutError: Could not hand the shortcut to the share sheet. Try again or open this page in Safari.
setup.shareHint: Tap Save to Files in the share sheet, then open the file in the Files app to add the shortcut.
setup.downloadHint: Open the downloaded file to add the shortcut.

accessHeaders.title: Cloudflare Access (optional)
accessHeaders.description: Fill these in only if a service such as Cloudflare Access sits in front of this instance and asks for a login before it lets requests through. The shortcut then sends the service token's Client ID and Client secret as the CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers, and the setup code carries them. If nothing protects your instance, leave both empty.
accessHeaders.clientIdPlaceholder: Enter the service token's Client ID
accessHeaders.clientIdStoredPlaceholder: Stored ({hint}). Enter a new ID to replace it
accessHeaders.clientIdStoredNoHintPlaceholder: Stored. Enter a new ID to replace it
accessHeaders.clientSecretPlaceholder: Enter the service token's Client secret
accessHeaders.clientSecretStoredPlaceholder: Stored. Enter a new secret to replace it
accessHeaders.bothRequired: Enter both the Client ID and the Client secret, or leave both empty.
accessHeaders.saveError: Could not save the Cloudflare Access headers
accessHeaders.loadError: Could not load the Cloudflare Access headers.

codeDialog.title: Your setup code
codeDialog.description: Copy the code, tap an Add shortcut button and paste the code when the shortcut asks for it. To set up another phone, scan the QR code and copy the text it shows.
codeDialog.warning: You won't see this code again. It holds a token that can add payments to your account, so don't share it. If you lose it, generate a new one.
codeDialog.qrLabel: QR code of the setup code
codeDialog.manualCopy: Tap and hold the code to copy it.

checklist.title: Then create the automation on your iPhone
checklist.description: iOS does not let apps share automations, so this part is done on the phone itself.
checklist.step1: Open Shortcuts, go to Automation, tap + and choose Transaction.
checklist.step2: Choose your cards, select Run Immediately and tap Next.
checklist.step3: Select the shortcut "MoneyMatter - Log card payment" and tap Done.
checklist.test: Run the shortcut by hand from the Shortcuts app. Without a payment it sends a test request and shows a notification that confirms the connection.

cardLinks.title: Card links
cardLinks.description: Apple Wallet gives each card a name. Link that name to the account its payments should be logged on. A card in several currencies can have an account for each currency and a default for the rest. A payment from a card without a link waits until you link it. Bank notifications name the card by its last digits, so add them too.

empty.title: No cards linked yet
empty.description: Link a card to the account its payments belong to. A payment from an unlinked card shows up below and waits.

dialog.description: Use the card name exactly as Apple Wallet shows it. Case and a trailing number such as •••• 1234 are ignored.

reasons.unknownCard: The card is not linked to an account.
reasons.rateUnavailable: There is no exchange rate for this payment's date.
reasons.processingFailed: MoneyMatter could not process this payment.
reasons.interrupted: Processing was interrupted before it finished.
reasons.emptyPayment: iOS sent no amount or merchant for this payment. Add it by hand.
reasons.rejected: This payment was refused as invalid.
reasons.unknownAccount: No account matches this payment. Link the card above and retry, or pick an account in the inbox.
reasons.sourceNotApproved: The app or sender is not approved yet. Approve it under the sources above, or mute it.
reasons.aiUnavailable: No AI model is available to read this notification. Retry once one is set up.
reasons.aiCapReached: The monthly AI limit is reached. Retry after it resets or once you raise it.
reasons.aiLimitReached: The daily limit for reading notifications is reached. Retry tomorrow.
reasons.aiQuotaWait: The AI model is out of reach right now. MoneyMatter retries automatically.
reasons.ownTransfer: This looks like a transfer between your own accounts. Log it anyway, or settle it in the inbox.
reasons.lowConfidence: MoneyMatter is not sure this is a payment. Log it if it is, or dismiss it.
reasons.holdReleased: A hold and its release cancelled each other out, so nothing was logged.
reasons.unverifiedParse: The amount MoneyMatter read is not in the notification text. Check it, then log it or dismiss it.

ignored.declined: Read as a declined payment, so nothing was logged.
ignored.security: Read as a security message, such as a code, so nothing was logged.
ignored.promo: Read as a promotion, so nothing was logged.
ignored.info: Read as information without a payment, so nothing was logged.
ignored.other: Not a payment, so nothing was logged.
ignored.contextRepeat: Another notification of an order that was already added, so nothing changed.
ignored.contextNoteKept: The payment already has your note, so nothing was added.
ignored.contextUnreadable: The text could not be read as an order, so nothing was added.
ignored.contextExpired: No payment came in time, so nothing was added.
ignored.contextConfirmed: The payment was already confirmed, so nothing was changed.
ignored.exchangeNoted: The message confirmed the currency exchange and gave it a note, so nothing else was added.

reasons.parkedTwin: The same payment was already waiting on another request, so this one joined it.
reasons.conversionLeg: This was one side of a currency exchange that waited on another request, so this one joined it.

iosAutomation.limitation: The iOS 26 shortcut logs contactless taps in a shop only. Payments inside apps and on websites do not trigger the Wallet automation; on iOS 27 or later the notifications from Wallet and your bank log them too. Otherwise log them by hand or connect your bank to bring them in with the bank sync.

payments.title: iOS 27 or later
payments.summary: One shortcut with built-in triggers. It logs Apple Pay taps and online payments from Wallet, and bank notifications: app pushes, SMS and email.

tap.title: iOS 26 or earlier
tap.summary: Logs Apple Pay taps in shops. It runs from a Wallet Transaction automation that you create on the phone.

choice.unavailable: This instance does not ship the "{name}" shortcut. Build it by hand with the manual guide above, or ask the administrator to ship the shortcut file.
choice.hint: Copy the setup code first. The shortcut asks for it once, when you add it. The button saves the shortcut file; open it from the Files app to add it to Shortcuts.

triggered.title: Then switch on the triggers on your iPhone
triggered.description: The shortcut brings its own triggers, one for Wallet payments and one for notifications. iOS adds them switched off.
triggered.step1: Add the shortcut: save the file, open it from the Files app and paste the setup code when it asks for it.
triggered.step2: Open the shortcut, tap each of its two triggers (Transaction and Notification) and turn on Automation. Imported triggers arrive switched off, so nothing runs until you do. Choose Run Immediately for both.
triggered.step3: The Notification trigger comes with Wallet and Messages already selected. Open it and add your bank apps, and your mail app if your bank writes by email.
triggered.step4: Apple Wallet may be missing from the Notification trigger after the import. If you do not see it in the list of apps, add it by hand.
triggered.gate: Only notifications that show an amount leave your phone. The check is a built-in Match Text, so no Apple Intelligence is needed.
triggered.test: Run the shortcut by hand from the Shortcuts app. It sends a test request and shows a notification that confirms the connection.

gate.title: Amount check
gate.description: Before a notification leaves your phone, the shortcut checks that it shows an amount, and the server checks it again. A stricter level sends less text, a looser one catches more payments.
gate.loadError: Could not load the amount check.
gate.saveError: Could not change the amount check

strict.title: Strict
strict.description: Only text with a currency code or symbol next to the number, like 43.60 GEL or $12.

standard.title: Standard
standard.description: Also local currency words, with a code, symbol or word within a few characters of the number.

loose.title: Loose
loose.description: Also a number with two decimals and no currency, like 43.60.

gate.looseWarning: The loose level also lets through messages that have only a number like 12.50, such as promos and delivery notes, so more unrelated text leaves your phone.
gate.newCodeHint: The level is part of the shortcut. Generate a new setup code and add the shortcut again to apply it.

sources.title: Notification sources
sources.description: Apps that sent notifications. Wallet and other known sources are trusted from the start, you approve the rest. Delivery and shopping apps are read as context: they add the store to the payment they belong to. Mute a source to ignore its notifications.
sources.loadError: Could not load the notification sources.
sources.empty: No sources yet. They appear after the first notification arrives.
sources.released: {count} waiting payment is being logged on this account. | {count} waiting payments are being logged on this account.

forgetDialog.title: Forget this source?
forgetDialog.description: {name} counts as a new source the next time it sends a notification. Payments already logged stay as they are.

sources.contextHint: Its notifications add the store to the payment they belong to. They never create a payment.

addContext.title: Add a context source by name
addContext.description: For an app or a sender that has not sent anything yet. For a messaging or mail app, name the sender too: the shortcut then sends only that sender’s notifications.
